Definition: Body/facial orientation vector measured in SCREEN coordinates (not world coordinates). Answers "which way is this character pointing at the viewer" — the axis that stays true across cuts.
Prompt phrasing (NL / MJ / SD / CN-API): NL: "facing screen-left, three-quarter view"; MJ: "3/4 view facing left"; SD: "(looking left:1.3), profile"; CN: "身体转向画面左侧，七分身侧脸"
Validator rule: OR-04: must not contradict motion_vector in the same panel (away-from-camera + toward-camera is impossible)
Fail mode: Position is correct but orientation is random, so the reader cannot tell who is addressing whom
Fix protocol: Write exactly ONE facing token per character per panel. Never stack two orientation words. In multi-character panels assign facing per character independently.

Allowed values: enter-left / enter-right / exit-left / exit-right / lateral-left / lateral-right / advance / retreat / static
Definition: Displacement of the character inside the frame between two beats — direction plus whether the movement enters, crosses or exits the frame.
Prompt phrasing (NL / MJ / SD / CN-API): NL: "walks left to right across the frame"; MJ: "motion blur to the right"; SD: "(running right:1.2)"; CN: "自画面左侧入画，向右横移"
Validator rule: OR-02: adjacent reversal requires a turn shot; OR-04: angle against facing must stay <=90 degrees
Fail mode: Direction flips between panels (walking right, then suddenly walking left) — reads as teleportation
Fix protocol: Add "motion direction: [token]" to every action beat. When a reversal is intended, insert a dedicated turn panel.

Definition: Which side of the 180-degree axis the camera sits on. A and B are defined by the left-right positions established in the first panel of the scene.
Prompt phrasing (NL / MJ / SD / CN-API): Do NOT describe it in the image prompt. Record it as a shot note; only crossing is written as a camera instruction ("camera arcs across the axis").
Validator rule: OR-03: A-side -> B-side direct cut is an axis jump; crossing must be bound to a transition panel
Fail mode: Left-right relationship flips and the reader loses spatial orientation
Fix protocol: Insert a neutral shot (frontal / symmetrical over-the-shoulder), or declare crossing and write the camera move.

Allowed values: Rule — facing change between adjacent panels
Definition: A facing sign change (3q-left -> 3q-right) must be motivated by a turn shot or a neutral panel.
Prompt phrasing (NL / MJ / SD / CN-API): Turn panel phrasing: "turning her body toward screen-right"
Validator rule: Adjacent panels have opposite facing signs and no turn shot in between
Fix protocol: Insert one turn panel, or add "turning her head" to the flipping panel.

Definition: Consecutive beats must not reverse the x-component without a motivated turn.
Validator rule: x-component sign flips between consecutive panels
Fix protocol: Insert a turn shot, or rewrite the second beat as same-direction continuation.

Definition: camera_side may only change through neutral or crossing. Crossing is the only place where a spatial rule is explicitly overridden.
Prompt phrasing (NL / MJ / SD / CN-API): Crossing phrasing: "the camera arcs around them as they turn"
Validator rule: Adjacent panels go A-side -> B-side with no neutral or crossing panel
Fail mode: Reader loses spatial anchor; dialogue sides become ambiguous
Fix protocol: Add a neutral panel; or mark crossing and write the camera movement in the same prompt.

Definition: Facing and motion must not contradict. away-from-camera together with toward-camera is physically impossible.
Prompt phrasing (NL / MJ / SD / CN-API): Backward walking must be explicit: "walking backwards, still facing the camera"
Validator rule: Same panel pairs away-from-camera with toward-camera
Fix protocol: Keep one of the two; if retreat is intended, state "walking backwards" verbatim.

Definition: Close-up and extreme close-up cannot carry orientation information. Facing must be established in a wider shot and merely inherited here.
Prompt phrasing (NL / MJ / SD / CN-API): Close-up prompt carries face only: "eyes and mouth, no body orientation"
Validator rule: Panel shot scale is close-up/ECU and it is the only source of facing in the sequence
Fail mode: Reader assumes the character changed pose
Fix protocol: Establish facing in an adjacent wider shot; keep the close-up to facial detail.

Definition: In a panel with three or more characters the facing set must not be uniform. Identical facing turns a group into a static chorus with no relational tension.
Prompt phrasing (NL / MJ / SD / CN-API): At least one character on 3q or profile while others differ
Validator rule: Panel has >=3 characters and the facing value set size is 1
Fix protocol: Give at least one character 3q-left or profile to build a triangle of vectors.

Definition: A character facing away cannot carry a speech bubble — the reader cannot attribute the line.
Prompt phrasing (NL / MJ / SD / CN-API): Move the line to a narration box, or turn the character to 3q
Validator rule: Panel has facing=away-from-camera and a speech bubble attached to that character
Fix protocol: Switch to 3q/profile, or convert the line into a narration box.

Allowed values: Rule — angle against the gaze chain
Definition: The gaze target must fall within 90 degrees of the facing vector; beyond that the reader cannot reconstruct who is looking at whom. Cross-check the gaze chain field in MultiCharacterSpatialRelations.
Validator rule: Facing vector and gaze vector diverge by more than 90 degrees
Fix protocol: Rotate facing toward the gaze target, or split the beat into two panels.

Definition: One orientation state per shot. Frame-level description does not exist as a control channel; video models only accept orientation change points along the timeline (Kling beat markers, Sora causal paragraphs, Seedance world logic).
Prompt phrasing (NL / MJ / SD / CN-API): Describe at most one change per 2-3 seconds
Validator rule: A single shot prompt contains more than two distinct facing values
Fail mode: Token dilution; anchor sentences get ignored
Fix protocol: Split into two shots instead of packing the change into one paragraph.

Definition: Tokens are lowercase kebab-case and must come from OrientationTokenBank. Free-text orientation phrases are not valid input anywhere in this standard.
Validator rule: Token does not exist in OrientationTokenBank
Fix protocol: Only use literal values listed in OrientationTokenBank.
